thread:
maria: :rotating_light: getting alerted — several hosted inference customers reporting 503s and long queue times starting ~15:42 UTC. Seen spike in upstream worker exits.

josh: can you paste the top log for one of the failing workers?

maria: grab from host gpu-az2-17, tail: 
```
Mar 17 15:42:12 infer-runner[2345]: runtime: received SIGKILL (exit code 137)
Mar 17 15:42:12 kernel: Out of memory: Killed process 2345 (infer-runner) total-vm:2560000kB, anon-rss:2400000kB, file-rss:0kB
Mar 17 15:42:12 nvidia: GPU 0: Xid 79: GPU has fallen off the bus.
```

dani: customer-facing: they see errors on bulk embed requests, timeouts ~10s then 503s. Affects ~120 requests/min for that org.

ben: sounds like GPU OOM + driver reset (Xid 79). Is this single-host or multi-host?

maria: initial signal from one host, but autoscaler routed more work there and then other hosts hit similar issues ~2m later.

carla: @ben can you check node eviction logs and kube events? Might be container runtime restarting loop.

ben: grabbing events: 
```
kubectl -n hosted logs pod/infer-xx -c runner --since=10m
Events:
  Warning  OOMKilling  3m   kubelet  Pod triggered OOMKill in container runner
  Normal   Killing     3m   kubelet  Killing container with id docker://runner:Container failed liveness probe
```

josh: any coredumps? `coredumpctl` shows nothing on host; container didn't produce core. We do have `dmesg` entries for GPU reset.

maria: nvidia-smi shows memory fragmentation before reset: `nvidia-smi dmon` captured rising mem util then abrupt 0 after reset.

dani: customer asks if this is related to their prompt sizes — they sent long prompt batches last hour. We should confirm batching behavior.

josh: checking runner metrics: batch size spiked to 48 on that model, sequence len ~2k tokens; mem per-shard reached near capacity. Autoscaling allowed burst routing to nodes with insufficient GPU headroom.

carla: short-term mitigation: reduce max_batch for that model route to 8 and enable fallback to CPU-based small model variant. Can someone push policy?

ben: I can patch routing policy: set max_batch=8 for route customer-prod until next deploy. Also add a hard cap on concurrent streams per-GPU. Pushing now.

maria: pushing runbook steps: collect /var/log/messages, `kubectl describe pod`, `nvidia-smi -q` snapshots, and sample request traces for customers impacted. Use tag incident.gpu-thrash.

josh: also recommend adding kernel param to log OOM killer backtraces and capture container memory cgroup stats: `cat /sys/fs/cgroup/memory/kubepods/.../memory.usage_in_bytes` right after an event.

dani: I told customer we throttled batch size and enabled fallback; will update if errors persist. They asked about billing credits — flagged to CS and finance.

ben: host patch applied. I'll cordon gpu-az2-17 and drain to avoid further noisy restarts while we debug.

incident-bot: automated: rollback watch for model route change deployed by ben at 15:51 UTC — route max_batch updated.

maria: after patch, 503s dropped to baseline within 90s. Still seeing 1-2 transient resets on other zones.

josh: next actions: 1) collect full driver logs and upload to /incidents/2473007890/artifacts, 2) reproduce with a controlled batch-size + seq-len test on dev cluster, 3) evaluate whether quantized model introduces different memory pressure.

carla: created follow-up ticket INFR-7642 for long-term fixes: smarter routing by per-request estimated mem, add preflight resource checks, and improve graceful fallback.

maria: tagging oncall handoff notes. If we see repeat within 24h escalate to Platform Eng for a kernel/driver deep dive. :thumbsup:

dani: customer confirms errors resolved for now, wants postmortem and potential credit. I'll coordinate.

ben: saving collected snapshots in S3: s3://redwood-incidents/2473007890/{dmesg,nvidia-smi,events}.

josh: repro plan attached (short): run loadgen with model X, batch sizes [8,24,48], seq lens [512,1024,2048], monitor GPU mem, driver logs, and trigger success/failure matrix.

maria: closing Slack thread for now — leaving monitoring on for 2h. Will reopen if errors reappear.

carla: thanks team. Good response.
